title: Pickleball for Beginners: Rules, Gear and Costs
seoTitle: Pickleball for Beginners: Rules, Gear and Costs
excerpt: New to pickleball? Learn the rules, beginner gear, current India equipment prices, the kitchen and two-bounce rule, plus tips for your first game.
content:
Pickleball is a paddle sport played on a compact court with a perforated plastic ball. It combines elements of tennis, badminton and table tennis, but it has its own court layout and rules. You can play singles or doubles, and many beginners find it approachable because the court is smaller than a tennis court and the basic rules are straightforward.

What Is Pickleball?

Pickleball was created in 1965 on Bainbridge Island, Washington, by Joel Pritchard, Bill Bell and Barney McCallum. The game developed from improvised equipment and a badminton court. Today, players use a solid paddle and a lightweight ball with holes. The standard court measures 20 feet wide by 44 feet long, the same dimensions for singles and doubles.

Pickleball is not simply a smaller version of tennis. Its two-bounce rule and non-volley zone, usually called the kitchen, shape the way rallies develop. Players use placement, patience and controlled shots as well as power.

How Is Pickleball Different from Tennis?

Pickleball uses a solid paddle instead of a strung racquet and a perforated plastic ball instead of a felt-covered tennis ball. The court is 20 by 44 feet, while a standard tennis court is much larger. The pickleball net is 36 inches high at the sidelines and 34 inches at the center.

The seven-foot non-volley zone on each side of the net is another major difference. A player may enter this area, but cannot volley the ball while standing in it or touching its line. The rule also applies if the player's momentum after a volley carries them into the zone.

What Equipment Do Beginners Need?

You can start with three essentials: a pickleball paddle, a ball suited to the playing surface, and access to a court. Many clubs and recreation centers lend or rent equipment, so try a session before buying a full kit.

  • Paddle: Choose a comfortable, beginner-friendly paddle with a grip that fits your hand. A balanced paddle with a generous hitting area can make it easier to control the ball.
  • Ball: Outdoor balls generally have smaller, more numerous holes and are designed for outdoor play. Indoor balls are usually softer and have fewer, larger holes. Use the type intended for your court and session.
  • Shoes: Court or tennis shoes with good lateral support are preferable to running shoes because pickleball involves quick side-to-side movement.
  • Clothing and water: Wear comfortable sports clothing and bring water. Sunglasses and a cap can help for outdoor sessions.

There is no single price that applies across India. Paddle material, brand, quality, ball type and retailer all affect the cost. Before purchasing, compare current local prices, check whether a club provides loan equipment, and avoid spending on advanced paddles until you know what feels comfortable.

How Much Does It Cost to Play?

Your main costs are equipment and court access. You may be able to try pickleball at a community event or club using borrowed equipment. If you play regularly, you may choose to buy a paddle and balls and pay for court bookings, coaching or club membership.

In India, court fees and equipment prices vary by city and facility. Ask the venue whether the booking fee includes paddles and balls, whether the court is shared, and whether beginner coaching is available. This is more reliable than assuming one national price range.

To give beginners a realistic starting point, the Hundred Spirit X Wide paddle is listed at ₹1,990 on Hundred's India store (as of 25 November 2026), and a six-pack of Cosco Pro 40 pickleballs is listed at ₹594 on Cosco's official store (as of 25 November 2026). That makes an example equipment-only budget about ₹2,584 before delivery, footwear or court fees. These are examples, not required purchases; prices and availability can change, so confirm them with the retailer before ordering.

The Spirit X Wide has a broad paddle face, which the manufacturer describes as forgiving for newer players. If you are unsure what to buy, borrow or rent a paddle first and check whether the venue provides balls.

What Are the Basic Rules of Pickleball?

These are the core rules to understand before your first game. Tournament formats and some local recreational sessions may add specific procedures, so follow the event organizer's rules when they differ.

  1. Serve diagonally: Start each rally with a serve directed diagonally into the opposite service court. Under the standard volley-serve method, the paddle moves in an upward arc and the ball is contacted below waist level, with the paddle head below the wrist. A legal drop serve is also permitted under the rulebook.
  2. Follow the two-bounce rule: The receiving team must let the serve bounce before returning it. The serving team must then let that return bounce before hitting it. After those two bounces, either team may volley or play the ball after a bounce.
  3. Respect the kitchen: The non-volley zone extends seven feet from the net on each side. You may stand in it and hit a ball after it bounces, but you must not volley while touching the zone or its boundary line.
  4. Keep the ball in bounds: A ball landing on a boundary line is generally in, except that a serve landing on the non-volley-zone line is a fault.
  5. Win by two: Traditional games are usually played to 11 points, and a team must lead by at least two. In traditional side-out scoring, only the serving team scores points. Some events may use an approved alternative format, so check the format before play.

A fault, such as hitting the ball out, failing to return it, volleying from the kitchen, or breaking a serving rule ends the rally. The official rulebook explains the full list of faults and the details of service and scoring.

What Is the Kitchen Rule?

The kitchen is the informal name for the non-volley zone. It is not a no-entry area: players can step into it whenever they are not volleying. The restriction is on volleying the ball while in the zone, including touching the line. A player also commits a fault if the momentum from a volley carries them into the zone after the shot.

This rule encourages players to use controlled shots, including a soft shot called a dink, rather than standing at the net and volleying every ball. Learning to move safely around the kitchen line is one of the most useful skills for a new player.

Where Can You Play Pickleball in India?

Start by checking local sports clubs, multi-sport facilities, recreation centers, schools and community groups. Availability changes, so confirm that the venue has a marked pickleball court, suitable nets and equipment before traveling. Some facilities offer beginner sessions or open-play hours, which can be a friendly way to learn.

If a venue only has a tennis court, ask whether it has permission and equipment to mark temporary pickleball lines and set the net to the correct height. Do not assume every tennis court can be converted during normal bookings.

Is Pickleball Good Exercise?

Pickleball involves walking, short bursts of movement, changes of direction and hand-eye coordination. The amount of exercise depends on the length and intensity of the session, the player's fitness and whether the game is singles or doubles. It can be a fun way to be active, but it is not automatically low-risk or suitable for every person.

Warm up before playing, wear appropriate court shoes, take breaks and drink water. If you have an injury or a health concern that affects exercise, seek advice from a qualified health professional before starting.

How Did Pickleball Get Its Name?

Pickleball was invented in 1965, but the origin of its name has often been debated. USA Pickleball's historical account says Joan Pritchard named the game after the “pickle boat” in crew racing, a boat made up of leftover rowers. The popular story that the game was named after the family dog, Pickles, is disputed; USA Pickleball's account says the dog was born after the game had already been named.

For a beginner, the important point is that the sport began as a family game made with improvised equipment and developed into a sport with an established court and rulebook.

Beginner Tips for Your First Game

  • Learn the two-bounce rule before trying to move quickly to the net.
  • Use a relaxed grip and aim for control rather than hitting every ball hard.
  • Stay balanced and take small adjustment steps instead of reaching for every shot.
  • Call the score clearly before serving, and ask your partner or opponent if you are unsure of the serving order.
  • Be considerate on shared courts: wait for the previous game to finish and follow the venue's rotation system.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is pickleball easier to learn than tennis?

Many beginners find the smaller court and simple starter rules approachable. It still takes practice to develop consistent serves, court positioning and shot control.

Can I play pickleball without buying equipment?

Often, yes. Ask a local club or organizer whether they lend paddles and balls for introductory sessions.

Can pickleball be played as singles?

Yes. Pickleball can be played as singles or doubles. The court dimensions remain the same.

Can I stand in the kitchen?

Yes. You may stand in the non-volley zone, but you cannot volley the ball while touching the zone or its boundary line. You must also avoid being carried into it by momentum after a volley.

How many points do you need to win?

Traditional games are usually played to 11 points, with a two-point lead required. Some organized events use other approved formats, so check the competition rules.

How long does a game take?

Game length varies with the level of play, rally length and scoring format. Allow extra time for warm-up, changing ends and waiting for a court rather than relying on a fixed match duration.

Sources: USA Pickleball: Essential Rules Summary (as of November 2026); USA Pickleball: 2026 Official Rulebook (as of November 2026); USA Pickleball: How Pickleball Got Its Name (as of November 2026); U.S. House of Representatives: Inventor of Pickleball, Representative Joel Pritchard (as of November 2026).
